relevance_note: Natural-history cohort of genetically confirmed SSADH deficiency with per-patient ALDH5A1 genotypes: 'The study included the genetic information of 58 (1:1 male/female ratio) individuals from 50 unrelated families with 32 ALDH5A1 allelic variants'.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; no script was available, so the extraction was written by hand and every span was checked against the Markdown. Table 2 ('Allelic variants, zygosity, resultant proteins combination, and eventual protein impairment effect of the SSADHD patients included in the study') is the per-patient table; its first column ('Patient') holds bare numbers, so labels follow the v4 bare-number rule: 'Table 2 #1' ... 'Table 2 #58'. Its columns are 'Patient | Allele_1 | Allele_2 | Zygosity | Protein variants combination | Effect' and it is printed in two fragments (patients 1-29, then 30-58). The text's 'patients #1, #5, #11, ...' and '(patient # 19)' use the same identifiers. Spans taken from that table are single cells (the label cell, the printed cDNA, 'Homozygosis'/'Compound heterozygosis') because the Markdown conversion pads cells with long unstable space runs. Zygosity comes from each person's own Zygosity cell ('Homozygosis' -> homozygous, 'Compound heterozygosis' -> compound heterozygous); one row is emitted per (person, variant), so a homozygote has one row for the repeated variant. Consanguinity 'yes' only for the nine rows whose zygosity cell carries the asterisk defined by the legend '* Consanguinity.' (patients 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 29, 32, 33, 45). Sex, age, ethnicity and vital status are group-level only ('1:1 male/female ratio', 'participants' overall median (IQR) age at their first study visit was 9.8 (5.4-15.3) years'), so they are 'not reported' per person. 'No participant was born prematurely or had any perinatal complications' names the whole group explicitly, so 'born prematurely' and 'perinatal complications' are recorded as excluded for every participant with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. Table 4 is a group-level table of counts and means, not per-patient values, and contains no stacked ' / ' cell; nothing from it was assigned to individuals. The CSS quartile sentences name individuals explicitly ('patients #1, #5, #11, #12, #16, #23, #35, #36, #37, #47, #51, #53, #54' = mildest clinical severity; '#4, #14, #15, #18, #28, #29, #33, #34, #43, #44, #50, and #56' = most severely affected) and are recorded per person. Contradictions found in the paper: (1) patient 37's allele 1 is printed 'c.278C > T' while C93F is attributed to c.278G > T elsewhere; (2) the text writes 'The A173C substitution (c.517C > T)' while Table 1 and Table 2 print R173C; (3) the text writes 'the G520A substitution (c.1558G > C)' while Table 1, Table 3 and Table 2 print G520R; (4) patients 11 and 36 have 'G176E' in their Table 2 protein-combination cells while Table 1 prints G176R for c.526G > A; (5) patient 44's alleles are printed 'c608C > T' without a dot; (6) the paper states 58 participants but the text describes a 'patient # 59' (severe clinical picture including drug-resistant seizures, 'an additional non-sense mutation (c.1234C > T)'); two people are never merged, so #59 has its own row and the discrepancy is flagged here. Variant type is recorded only where the paper's own words give a class for that exact variant: 'splice' for the six variants it calls splice-site or splicing variants (c.1015-2A > C, c.870 + 3delA, c.1402 + 2T > C, c.870 + 1G > T, c.610-2A > G, c.1015-3C > G), 'nonsense' for c.1234C > T ('an additional non-sense mutation (c.1234C > T)') and for c.612G > A only in patient #1's sentence ('a combination of two nonsense variants'), 'missense' for c.1226 G > A, c.278G > T, c.803G > A and c.1005C > A (the missense-variant sentences of the quartile paragraph), and 'large deletion/CNV' for 'Deletion 6p22.3' ('An additional variant included the deletion of chromosome 6p22.3 in its entirety'). Otherwise 'not reported': Table 2's 'Truncated protein' and 'impaired splicing' describe the protein combination, not the class of an individual variant, and '23 non-sense (20%)' is a cohort-level allele count. protein_hgvs_as_stated is the protein string printed for that cDNA in Table 1's 'Protein Variant' column, exactly as printed (no 'p.' prefix was added; Table 1 prints 'Splice site' or 'No SSADH synthesis' for those entries, which are not p. descriptions, so the field is null there); c.278C > T is not printed in Table 1, so its protein is null. The paper prints no transcript and no genomic (g.) coordinates. Cohort-level pathogenicity ('the 32 allelic variants ... were pathogenic') and the SIFT/POLYPHEN-2/CUPSAT/BindProfX/SpliceAI/steric-hindrance results are computational predictions, not functional assays of a patient's variant, so pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors, functional_evidence_statement and acmg_criteria_as_stated are 'not reported' for every variant (D-29); inheritance and parental_testing_statement are 'not reported' because the paper reports no parental testing and no carrier parent. Table 1 appears in the Markdown as several fragments with the reference list interleaved inside the table; it was read for variant classes and protein strings but not transcribed. source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' throughout (these are the study's own patients and there is no per-patient source column). In the checklist, only patient # 59 has a non-'not reported' row ('drug-resistant seizures', recorded as 'seizures or epilepsy' observed, evidence_basis 'stated for this individual'); all other checklist rows are 'not reported'.
